chunks: By the same chain of narration, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Al-Nadr ibn Sawid, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Al-Ahwal, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) was asked about fasting two Thursdays with a Wednesday in between them.
He replied: As for Thursday, it is the day when deeds are presented; as for Wednesday, it is the day when Hell was created; and as for fasting, it is Paradise.
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of fasting on Thursdays and Weddays in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: In this narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal*, the Imam clarifies the metaphysical significance of Thursday as the day deeds are presented and Wednesday as the day Hell was created, linking these cosmic events to the spiritual efficacy of fasting. This tradition underscores the Shia emphasis on specific weekly days for spiritual reflection, positioning fasting not merely as ritual observance but as a direct means of attaining Paradise (Jannah).

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 7-82 By the same documentation it is narrated that Al-Hussein ibn Sa’id quoted Al-Nazr ibn Soweed, on the authority of Hisham ibn Salim, on the authority of Al-Ahval that Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB) said, “God’s Prophet(MGB) was questioned about fasting on two Thursdays and on the Wednesday in between them
He (MGB) replied, ‘Thursdays are the days when our deeds are presented and Wednesday is the day on which Hell was created. Fasting is an armor against the Fire.’”
